contents.title: Quiz Diagnostic 1ere Anglais - Serie 26
contents.subject: Anglais
contents.description: Diagnostic Anglais 1ere : Les modaux – capacité, permission, obligation

questions.question: Choose the correct modal to express a past ability: 'When she was young, she ___ play the piano beautifully.'
'You mustn't park here' means that parking is not necessary here.
Quelle est la différence de sens entre ces deux phrases ? 'You must wear a uniform at school.' / 'You should wear a uniform at school.'
Which sentence correctly asks for permission in a formal context?
'I don't have to work on Sundays' means that working on Sundays is forbidden.
Complète la phrase avec le bon modal et explique ton choix : 'You ___ (ne peux pas / il est interdit de) use your phone during the exam.'
Which sentence uses 'be able to' correctly in the future tense?
choices: She will can speak Spanish after the course.
She will be able to speak Spanish after the course.
She will could speak Spanish after the course.
She would able to speak Spanish after the course.

questions.question: 'Should' can be used to give advice or express a moral obligation.

exercisenotion.notion: Modaux de capacité : can, could, be able to
exercisenotion.description: Can exprime une capacité présente. Could exprime une capacité passée ou une demande polie. Be able to est plus formel et peut s'utiliser à tous les temps. Ex : I can swim / I could read at age 4 / I will be able to drive soon.

exercisenotion.notion: Modaux de permission : can, could, may, might
exercisenotion.description: Can/could demandent ou accordent une permission de façon informelle. May/might sont plus formels. Ex : Can/Could I open the window? May I leave early? Note : could et might sont plus polis que can et may.

exercisenotion.notion: Modaux d'obligation : must, have to, should, ought to, need to
exercisenotion.description: Must exprime une obligation forte souvent imposée par le locuteur. Have to exprime une obligation externe. Should/ought to donnent un conseil ou une obligation morale. Mustn't = interdiction. Don't have to = absence d'obligation.
